newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips further after weekend rain.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips further after weekend rain.

text.p: French new and old crop wheat prices slipped further on Monday after weekend rain brought some relief to thirsty crops.
But trade was limited as there will be no European Union weekly grain auction for the next two weeks due to public holidays in Belgium. The next meeting of the EU's grain committee will be on May 15.
Wheat into Rouen for May delivery was bid at 890 francs per tonne,excluding carry, down one franc from Friday.
Wheat into Rouen for September-December delivery fetched 900 francs, excluding carry, down five.
Wheat prices started their retreat on Friday as the weather broke and rain hit France's western coast.
News the European Union had reimposed a tax on wheat exports to keep domestic prices and supplies under control also put pressure on prices.
Weekend rain helped crop crospects in the main producing areas but more rain is needed after a three-month dry spell, farmers and crop experts said.
But a Meteo France forecaster has said the weather is set to turn dry again Wednesday and remain dry until Saturday.
"The rain did some good but it was not sufficient," a local ITCF crop expert for centre France and the Paris basin said.
Weekend rain was 10 mm across France but the Beauce grain belt got as much as 20 mm.
France's largest farm union FNSEA has said that even if water tables returned to normal the drought had now done irreversible damage to winter grain.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
For 1996/97, the charges are as follows (francs per tonne):
1st half 2nd half
August 3.64 7.27
September 10.91 14.54
October 18.18 21.81
November 25.45 29.09
